semaron.title: semaron encoding
intro: Semaron Kuriale is an alphabet of capital and small letters, written left to right. This encoding writes a roman spelling in its letters: `th` is one letter, `ch` is written with the letters for t, s and h, a doubled `a`, `i` or `u` is a long vowel, `q` is written as `k`, and `y` before a vowel is a glide. An apostrophe or hyphen after a letter writes the catch, a mark on the letter before it.

aelwythi-semaron.title: aelwythi-semaron encoding
intro: A second roman spelling for Semaron Kuriale, which draws the same letters as the semaron encoding. It takes each roman letter on its own where semaron joins them: a doubled vowel is two vowels, `c` is written as s before `e`, `i` and `y` and as k elsewhere, and `ch` and `tch` are written with the letters for t, s and h. The apostrophe and the quotation mark draw nothing and are written as invisible marks, and a hyphen draws a space and carries a mark.

pirzath.title: pirzath encoding
intro: Pirzath is a script of letters read left to right, drawn carved in Pirzath Carved and in a hand in Pirzath Hand on the same code points. This encoding writes a roman spelling in them: a digraph such as `th` or `kh` is a single letter, and `ay` before a consonant or at the end of a word is the single letter for the diphthong.

thuravark.title: thuravark encoding
intro: Thuravark Carved is a row of straight staves for letters, numerals and a few marks, read left to right. This encoding writes a roman spelling in them: a digraph such as `th` or `kh` is a single stave, a doubled vowel is the stave twice, and a hyphen draws nothing and is written as an invisible mark.

qalezu.title: qalezu encoding
intro: Qalezu Hand is a right-to-left script with one sign for each consonant. This encoding writes a roman spelling in them: a vowel draws nothing except at the start of a word, where it draws the catch sign; elsewhere it is written as an invisible mark, so decoding restores it, and a digraph such as `kh` is a single sign.

vedyakshara.title: vedyakshara encoding
intro: Vedyakshara Classical is a left-to-right script in which each consonant carries the vowel `a`. This encoding writes a roman spelling in it: a consonant before a vowel is the bare consonant followed by that vowel's sign, a consonant elsewhere is the consonant with the cut that takes the vowel away, and `a` draws no sign of its own and is written as an invisible mark.

helonika.title: helonika encoding
intro: Helonika Book is an alphabet of capital and small letters, written left to right. This encoding writes a roman spelling in its letters: `ei` and `ou` are the single letters for the long vowels, while `kh`, `zh` and doubled vowels are written as two letters.

helonika-bizarian.title: helonika-bizarian encoding
intro: A second roman spelling for Helonika Book. Here `kh` and `zh` are single letters, a doubled `a`, `i` or `u` is a long vowel, `ei` is two letters, and an acute vowel is the vowel followed by the accent mark.

helonika-bethuan.title: helonika-bethuan encoding
intro: A third roman spelling for Helonika Book. Here `kh` is a single letter and `zh` two, a doubled `a`, `i` or `u` is a long vowel, `ei` is the single letter for the long vowel, and an acute vowel is the vowel followed by the accent mark.

veldikko.title: veldikko encoding
intro: Veldikko is a right-to-left calligraphy whose letters join along the line, with vowel marks that float above them. This encoding writes a roman spelling in its code points: a letter, then the doubling bar if the consonant is doubled, then each vowel mark followed by its signs of length, pitch and emphasis.
structure: Its rows are generated from a small number of parts, so the complete table is too long to read. Every consonant is a single letter; a roman letter the script lacks (`b`, `f`, `w`, `z`, `c`, `q`, `g`) is written as the nearest letter, and `x` is written as two letters. A vowel is its vowel sign, and a vowel at the start of a word is written after the carrier letter. A doubled vowel adds the long sign. The accents circumflex, caron and acute, typed on a vowel or after it, add the rise, fall and emphasis signs. A doubled consonant adds the doubling bar. A capital draws the same letters as its small form and carries a mark that decoding reads back as the capital.
The rows below are the rows of a single character, then a few longer rows of each length.

veldikko-aelendi.title: veldikko-aelendi encoding
intro: A second roman spelling for Veldikko, with the same letters and marks. It writes the consonant digraphs such as `th`, `dh`, `kh` and `ng` as single letters.

zethu-mdc.title: zethu-mdc encoding
intro: Khelathi Zethu Glyphs is a right-to-left script of signs, one sign to a word. This encoding writes the named code of a sign, in capitals, as its code point.

chalish-ceremonial.title: chalish-ceremonial encoding
intro: Chalish Pilam Ceremonial is the carved hand of Ch'alish P'ilam, a logographic script whose glyphs compose into blocks. This encoding writes the named code of a glyph as its code point: a concept glyph by its name in capitals (`SUN`), a syllable sign by its syllable and number (`ka1`), and a number by `n` and its value (`n13`).

Inside a block, `*` writes the joiner that sets two items side by side and `:` the joiner that stacks the first over the second; the font lays the block out from them. A block ends wherever no joiner follows, so `-` and a space each write only their invisible mark. Zero and the places of the count have code points and no ceremonial drawing, so they print the box.

chalish-common.title: chalish-common encoding
intro: Chalish Pilam Common is a logographic script in which each glyph records a concept. This encoding writes the named code of a glyph, such as `n1` for the numeral one, as its code point.
